key_insight: Radiology vision foundation models are rapidly advancing, but the field is still fragmented in data, methods, and validation.
clinical_relevance: These models may eventually improve imaging workflows and downstream tasks, but current evidence is not yet strong enough for broad clinical deployment.
method: Scoping review of peer-reviewed studies from January 2017 to March 2026
Included 67 studies training foundation models exclusively on radiological imaging data
Mapped evidence across data scale/heterogeneity, pretraining methodology, and transferability/generalization
evidence_signal: Studies ranged from under 100,000 samples to multi-million-image cohorts, with transformer-based self-supervised methods common, but cross-center and modality-shift evaluation was inconsistently reported.
watch_item: Clinical translation is limited by uneven data representativeness, heterogeneous benchmarks, and incomplete deployment-oriented validation.
paper_title: Vision Foundation Models in Radiology: A Scoping Review of Data, Methodology, Evaluation and Clinical Translation
